question: How does a small language model relate to a large one, according to the lecture?

options.text: The same architecture throughout, with fewer stacks and smaller layers inside them
options.feedback: A small model has the same attention-plus-MLP (multi-layer perceptron) stacks, just fewer of them and smaller. Its JPEG of the world is blurrier, and the trade is that it fits on hardware you carry, such as a laptop or a phone.

options.text: A simpler architecture that leaves out the MLP (multi-layer perceptron) layers to save space
options.feedback: Dropping the MLP would drop the model's world knowledge entirely, and no model does that. Small models keep every part of the architecture; each part is just smaller.

options.text: The same model with its vocabulary cut down to the most common words
options.feedback: The vocabulary is not where the size lives. What shrinks in a small model is the parameter count in the MLPs (multi-layer perceptrons) and the number of decoder stacks.

options.text: A large model with most of its decoder stacks skipped at run time to save memory
options.feedback: A small model is built and trained small; it is not a large one with parts switched off mid-run. It has fewer stacks and smaller MLPs (multi-layer perceptrons) from the start.
